analyticalQuestion: Where exactly does the active induced column cross one, is that root unique, and do all other charge sectors stay strictly below it throughout the adjacent millionth window?
supportedClaim: For the reduced canonical edge generating system with kappa=3/4, the active true column C_r(81,162) defines a degree-80 threshold polynomial P(r)=C_r(81,162)-1 with 80 strictly positive nonconstant coefficients. Its globally unique positive root satisfies 0.376932499290527340<r_*<0.376932499290527341. An exact 81-polynomial Sturm sequence independently counts one root in that interval. Across [0.376932,0.376933], an exact monotone sandwich keeps all 243 competing columns and sectors below the active column; the nearest competitor is s=164 with a strict gap of approximately 9.9933786489298977945e-05. Hence the current induced two-block weighted-l1 norm is below one, equal to one, and above one below, at, and above r_* within this window, without implying a PDE singularity or a result on three-dimensional Navier-Stokes regularity.
